description: Experience the authentic taste of San Francisco with this classic Sourdough Boule, renowned for its distinct tangy flavor and irresistible chewy crumb. A perfectly golden, crackly crust gives way to a soft, airy interior, making it ideal for any meal or simply enjoyed with butter. This recipe guides you to bake a masterpiece that captures the essence of traditional American artisan bread.

instructions.title: Mix the Dough (Autolyse & Final Mix)
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water, bread flour, and whole wheat flour. Mix until no dry spots remain, forming a shaggy dough. Cover and let it rest for 30 minutes (autolyse). After the autolyse, add the active sourdough starter and salt. Mix thoroughly with your hands, squeezing and folding the dough until the starter and salt are fully incorporated. The dough will be sticky.

instructions.title: Bulk Fermentation with Stretch and Folds
instructions.text: Cover the bowl and let the dough bulk ferment at room temperature (72-78F) for 3-4 hours. During this time, perform 3-4 sets of stretch and folds every 30-45 minutes. To do a stretch and fold, wet your hand, grab a portion of the dough, stretch it upwards, and fold it over itself. Rotate the bowl and repeat 3-4 times until all sides have been stretched and folded. The dough should become smoother and more elastic.

instructions.title: Pre-Shape the Dough
instructions.text: Lightly flour your work surface. Gently turn the dough out onto the surface. Using a bench scraper, gently shape the dough into a loose round or rectangle. Allow it to rest uncovered for 20-30 minutes. This helps the gluten relax and makes the final shaping easier.

instructions.title: Final Shape and Cold Proof
instructions.text: Lightly flour your hands and the dough. Gently shape the dough into a tight boule (round) or batard (oval) using tension to create a smooth surface. Transfer the shaped dough, seam-side up, into a floured banneton basket or a bowl lined with a floured kitchen towel. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 12-18 hours for a slow cold proof. This develops flavor and makes the dough easier to score.

instructions.title: Preheat Oven and Dutch Oven
instructions.text: About 45 minutes before baking, place a Dutch oven with its lid into your oven and preheat to 475F (245C). Ensure the Dutch oven is fully preheated to achieve the best oven spring and crust.

instructions.title: Bake the Boule
instructions.text: Carefully remove the hot Dutch oven from the oven. Gently invert the cold dough from the banneton directly into the hot Dutch oven. Score the top of the dough with a sharp razor blade or lame in your desired pattern. Place the lid back on and bake for 30 minutes. Remove the lid and continue to bake for another 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is deeply golden brown and caramelized. The internal temperature should be around 200-210F (93-99C).

instructions.title: Cool Completely
instructions.text: Carefully remove the baked sourdough boule from the Dutch oven and transfer it to a wire rack. Allow the bread to cool completely for at least 1-2 hours before slicing. Slicing too early can result in a gummy texture and flatten the crumb.

tips: Ensure your sourdough starter is active and bubbly; a healthy starter is key to good rise and flavor.
Do not skip the cold proofing step; it greatly enhances the flavor, crust development, and makes the dough easier to handle and score.
Always allow your freshly baked sourdough to cool completely on a wire rack before slicing to prevent a gummy texture and preserve its open crumb.
